attrs.goal: Pass through a repo that turns change-risk review off, and keep its merge conditions
Read the change risk of the branch, and select its approval rule and its next extra role

attrs.label: Classify change risk
attrs.prompt: Classify the change risk of the branch for the handoff $context.handoff. The path floor is `$context.change_risk_floor`. The rubric is `$context.rubric` in the repo. The draft $context.draft holds the Door and the Blast Radius.

attrs.label: Check change risk
attrs.prompt: The change-risk classifier gave the branch for the handoff $context.handoff the change risk `low`: $context.change_risk_reason Check whether the branch needs a human approval anyway. The rubric is `$context.rubric` in the repo. The draft $context.draft holds the Door and the Blast Radius.

attrs.label: Extra review
attrs.prompt: Review the head of the pull request $context.pr_url as the $context.extra_role role, before its final review. The approval rule of its change risk $context.change_risk names this role. Take clean when nothing must change before the merge. Otherwise write each finding as a row of a batch file, report CONTEXT: batch=<path>, and take findings. The receiver triages each row, the implementer fixes each confirmed row, and you review the new head.

attrs.label: Extra triage
attrs.prompt: Triage the findings of the $context.extra_role role on the head of $context.pr_url, in $context.batch, as the Extra review section of your instructions says.

attrs.label: Approvals held
attrs.prompt: The pull request $context.pr_url needs $context.approvals_needed before it merges, and its change risk names no reviewer to ask. A new approval on the PR answers recheck. Answer recheck to count the approvals again, or report to end at the final report.

attrs.label: Second review
attrs.prompt: Review the pull request $context.pr_url before it merges. Its change risk is $context.change_risk, and its merge needs $context.approvals_needed. Answer approve to approve it, or say what to change.

attrs.label: Second reply
attrs.prompt:
The second reviewer answered the review of $context.pr_url with a reply that is not the approve option:

$human.gate.text

This reply approves nothing, also when it says that the reviewer approves. When it asks for changes, write each change as a row of a batch file, report CONTEXT: batch=<path>, and take changes. Otherwise take ask_again, and the reviewer gets the review again.

$context.settled

Draft PR
attrs.prompt: Stage 4. Draft the pull request for the handoff $context.handoff, as the pr skill says. Pass the evidence of each Done when item and the verifier's verdicts in $context.verdicts. Write the draft as a JSON file of `title`, `body` and `vars`, and report CONTEXT: draft=<path>. `body` is the summary text that the template takes as input, not the rendered body. `vars` holds a text value for each variable that `workcell tool pr open --template` marks required. Add `attach`, a list of paths under `.devkit/proof/`, when you have proof media. Embed each file under the line it proves, as an image or a link of its attach path, or leave it out of `attach`. Never commit proof media. The PR draft section of your instructions says how. When the branch holds no commit because a human entry of the decision record decides to change no code, draft nothing: report LABEL: no_code and CONTEXT: decision=D<n>, the id of that entry.

$context.gate_output

Fix the cause on the branch. Commit every change, so the tree is clean. The open stage pushes the branch. Then report done. Do not wait for a low machine load or for other suites to stop.

attrs.label: Fix
attrs.prompt: Apply the review batch in $context.batch to the branch of $context.pr_url. Commit each row that asks for a change. A `Refuted` row, an `Ask` row and an `L` row ask for no change, unless a person picked the row: report each of them as `<row id>: not applied: <verdict>`. A row that changes the PR title or body changes the draft $context.draft: the engine writes the draft into the open PR before the next review. A draft with `"rendered": true` holds the title and the whole PR body as the run read them at its start. The engine replaces the whole body with it, so a change that a person or a bot made to the body after that read is lost. Do not push: the engine pushes the branch after your report. Report each commit under its row id, on a line of its own, as `<row id>: <short sha> <subject>`, and a row that you did not apply as `<row id>: not applied: <reason>`. The engine replies to the review comment of each row with that commit or that reason. Report LABEL: fixed after the last commit.

attrs.label: Start
Report
attrs.prompt: Write the final report for issue $context.issue, as the Final report section of your instructions says, and publish it with workcell tool run report. The record of the rows that the pre-PR cap left is `$context.left_rows`. When that is not empty, pass it to that command as --left-rows <record>. The file of the owner's answers and the fix commits of the rows is `$context.left_answers`. When that is not empty, pass it to that command as --left-answers <file>. The report then shows each answer beside its row or takes a settled row out of Left for you, and the run asks the owner no question about that row. The verify line is $context.verify_line. The answers to the Important Questions are in $context.conceptual_answers. A run that stopped short has the stopped line $context.stopped, which the report shows and records with workcell tool run status report $context.issue --stopped. A merged pull request has the Merge line merged $context.merge_sha. A merge that did not land has the merge result $context.merge_result, and the Merge line not merged: <that reason>. A rebase result of STACKED in $context.rebase_result means that the run skipped a rebase because the branch is stacked on an unmerged branch, and the report names that skip. A merge result of BASE-MOVED or CONFLICT with a rebase result of CONFLICT or IN-PROGRESS means that the rebase onto the moved base stopped on a conflict and the run skipped it. The report names that skipped conflicted rebase, and the conflict reason of a CONFLICT merge result. Then report done. When the report needs the human, the run asks them next.

attrs.label: Left for you
attrs.prompt:
The final report of issue $context.issue leaves rows for you. The report on $context.pr_url shows each row in full. The rows are:

$context.report_asks

Reply with the numbers of the rows you pick and what to do with each. You can also set a round limit or raise the stop stage. When a limit stopped the run, you can answer retry to push any commit that the stop left off the pull request, wait for CI and bots on the head again, and start each count again.

attrs.label: Take pick
attrs.prompt:
The human answered the final report of issue $context.issue, whose fields are in $context.report_fields:

$human.gate.text

Follow the Human picks section of your instructions and take the pick: rounds_raised, rounds_noted, raised_pr, raised_review, raised_merge, squash, decided, rebased, rerun_review, rerun_skills, retry, limit_reached or done. A pick that raises the stop stage also reports CONTEXT: through=<the new stage>.
